**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Coordinate image pulls with other cluster downloads**

Fresh evidence after the earlier concurrency fix is that this share is scoped only to one `pull_image_on_nodes` invocation and never acquires VirtualNAS's `_dispatched_download_lock`. If a one-node image pull runs while a capped weight download targets another node—or two image-pull requests target disjoint nodes—each operation receives the full controller cap, so a 100 Mbps setting permits roughly 200 Mbps. Serialize all controller-dispatched internet operations behind one coordinator or allocate shares across active operations.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scale the remote patch deadline with the forwarded cap**

When a remote patch build must pull an uncached base image under a low cap, forwarding the cap here can make the pull legitimately exceed `_remote`'s unchanged two-hour deadline (`deadline = time.monotonic() + 7200`). At 0.1 Mbps, two hours transfers only about 90 MB, so ordinary base images cause the controller job to fail while the agent continues building. Derive the polling deadline from the cap and expected image size, or keep polling while the remote job reports progress.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor NO_PROXY when chaining registry traffic**

Fresh evidence after adding upstream-proxy chaining is that only `HTTPS_PROXY` is forwarded, while `NO_PROXY` is neither passed nor evaluated by the limiter. On hosts that require the corporate proxy for internet access but exclude an internal, TLS-valid registry via `NO_PROXY`, every capped pull is still sent to the corporate proxy and can be rejected even though the ordinary direct pull works. Pass the bypass list into the limiter and dial matching registry authorities directly.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve parallel downloads when the cap is disabled**

This lock is acquired unconditionally, including when `max_download_bandwidth_mbps` is the default `0`. As a result, queue jobs targeting independent nodes that `_dispatch_loop` deliberately starts concurrently now wait behind one another, serializing otherwise unlimited full-model downloads; the selected-file path has the same unconditional lock. Acquire the cluster-wide lock only when the effective cap is positive.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Strip the bandwidth field before building the patch**

Whenever the controller targets only capable nodes, it adds `max_download_bandwidth_mbps` to this request—even when the configured cap is `0`. `_local` later passes the same dictionary to `build_patched_image`, whose `normalize_patch_request` rejects every key outside its patch-field allowlist, so all such local and agent-side builds fail with `Unsupported patch request fields` after any base pre-pull. Remove the coordination-only field before invoking the strict patch builder.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Route the size preflight through the limiter**

For every capped image pull, this inspect container receives only `HOME`; sharing the proxy's Docker network does not set `HTTPS_PROXY`, so Skopeo connects directly to the registry outside the token bucket. This also makes the preflight fail silently on proxy-only hosts, returning an unknown size and disabling both the staging-capacity check and determinate progress. Configure this container to use the already-running limiter proxy just like the copy container.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve trust for registries using a private CA**

When a secure private registry uses a CA installed under the Docker daemon's certificate configuration, it does not appear in `InsecureRegistryCIDRs`, so this still selects the isolated Skopeo path even though that container lacks the daemon's CA. Fresh evidence after the earlier trust fix is that the current implementation consults only `InsecureRegistryCIDRs`; capped pulls from privately certified registries therefore fail TLS verification while ordinary daemon pulls succeed.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Establish TLS when chaining through an HTTPS proxy**

When `HTTPS_PROXY` names a TLS-protected proxy such as `https://proxy.example:443`, this parser discards the scheme and `connect_target` sends a plaintext CONNECT request over a raw socket. Fresh evidence after the earlier proxy-chaining fix is that no TLS wrapping occurs after the scheme is removed, so capped pulls fail against HTTPS proxy endpoints even though the host's normal proxy-aware clients work.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
